questions.question: dashboard-manager passed on your two answers. Please confirm them here, because the reviewer won't accept a relayed ruling. First, Stop: a message still waiting for a stopped agent is marked FAILED and isn't delivered after a restart. It stays in that agent's inbox, and its sender gets a stored 'not delivered' notice. That's how comms works today; only the switch test changes. Is that what you meant?

options.label: Yes, failed + inbox (Recommended)
options.description: Keep today's behaviour. The test then checks that the message is marked failed, isn't delivered after the restart, and is still in the agent's inbox. No comms change is needed, so the new three-attempt switch run can start right away.

options.label: Cancelled, not failed
options.description: Mark it cancelled instead, so a Stop doesn't show up as an error. That's a small comms change plus review, about an hour more.

options.label: Deliver after restart
options.description: Keep the message and deliver it when the agent starts again. That changes comms and aify-env, about a day of work.

questions.question: Second, the 10 dead aify-env keys. Delete can't remove them: it deletes agents, and 33 of your 35 live agents also appear on those dead keys' lists. Nothing that exists clears a key, but a one-time manual cleanup can. I'd back up the comms database, delete the 10 dead keys and their rows, and restart the comms container; dashboard-manager does the same on the dashboard. That deletes data, so it needs your yes. Which do you want?

options.label: One-time cleanup (Recommended)
options.description: No new code. Back up, delete the 10 keys, restart comms; it takes minutes. If new dead keys turn up later, we repeat it or build the command then.

options.label: Build the retire command
options.description: A proper aify-env command, with a check in comms that refuses a key still reporting. About half a day plus review.

options.label: Leave them for now
options.description: After the switch, every agent listed on those keys reads 'unknown', and sends to them queue up.

questions.question: You asked what I think about the dead keys. They will come back, but rarely. A clean stop clears its key, but a crash, a forced kill or a power loss still leaves one, and that has happened on this PC before. Each one is costly after the switch: a dead key makes every agent it lists read 'unknown', even when a live key lists them too. dashboard-manager measured that today all 35 of your agents would read unknown. So my recommendation is no manual command. Instead, comms automatically ignores a key that has missed three of its own announced reporting intervals whenever a live key lists the same agent. Do the one-time cleanup of today's 10 keys now so the switch isn't blocked, and build the automatic rule right after the switch. The cleanup deletes data (backed up first), so it needs your yes. OK?

options.label: Cleanup now, auto-rule after (Recommended)
options.description: Back up the databases, remove the 10 dead keys in comms and the dashboard, restart the comms container, and check every agent reads correctly. The automatic rule follows as its own reviewed change after the switch.

options.label: Auto-rule before the switch
options.description: Build the automatic rule first and switch with it included. No manual delete, but the switch slips by roughly a day: the rule changes the status view, so the three-attempt switch run must happen again.

options.label: Cleanup only, no rule
options.description: Clean up today's 10 and do nothing more. Each later crash needs another manual cleanup, and until it's done all affected agents read unknown.

questions.question: You objected to restarting aify-env for the switch. It isn't an extra restart: the switch always needed your aify-env running current main. All testing happens in my sandboxes, not on your setup. The new part is only the order: aify-env must be on current code before comms switches. Your installed aify-env (2ae603d) doesn't report how often it reports. Under the switch, comms reads that as 'stopped reporting', so every agent would show 'unknown'. Which way do you want it?

options.label: Wait for my next restart (Recommended)
options.description: No forced restart. Whenever you next restart aify-env for your own reasons, it comes up on current main, and I switch comms right after. No extra code and no requalification; the switch date is just whenever that happens.

options.label: Restart once at switch time
options.description: You pick a moment, restart aify-env once (this restarts the managed agents), and I switch comms minutes later. No extra code, and the fastest switch.

options.label: Assume a 60 s default
options.description: comms assumes an old aify-env reports every 60 s, so no restart is needed for the switch. This reverses your 10-21 ruling that comms guesses no number, and the switch then has to be retested against your installed aify-env. Roughly a day's delay.
